newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight soars to 20 pct on liquidity squeeze.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight soars to 20 pct on liquidity squeeze.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate soared to as high as 20 percent from 8.5 percent on Thursday, triggered by a liquidity squeeze, dealers said on Friday.
They said the surge in rates was caused by offshore players scrambling for ringgit-funds.
"The overnight was earlier taken at 20 percent and is holding at 16-18 percent. I've not seen rates this high since the late 80s," said a senior dealer with a Malaysian bank.
One-week rate was also pushed higher, trading between 10 and 20 percent.
Dealers said if not for heavy lending by a large local bank, rates could have gone higher. The bank is believed to be acting for Bank Negara, they said.

Dealers said the jump was not surprising after a sharp outgo of ringgit from the market. The central bank had intervened aggreessively in the foreign exchange market on Wednesday to stem the slide of the ringgit, tightening the availability of the currency.
"Foreign banks were snapping up all the money on offer as many offshore players were short of ringgit,' said another local bank dealer.
One-month interbank rate ended at 8.5/9.0 percent against 7.55 on Thursday, and three-month was at 8.0/8.5 percent from 7.6.
Bank Negara said in a statement on Friday that the rise in money market rates was a temporary phenomenon.
It also said that its monetary policy stance remains unchanged.
The Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rates (KLIBOR) were refixed at 0830 GMT after the regular daily fixing at 0300 GMT was found to be sharply different from interbank dealing rates.
The benchmark three-month KLIBOR was refixed at 8.76 percent from 7.53 at 0300 GMT.
